description: Which path in this container persists, and where. This is the DECLARATION: it is the reviewed statement of what survives a wake, and it is what a change to the durable layout is argued against. It is not executed - `bin/dsh-state.sh` and `bin/dsh-provision.sh` name these paths directly, in one constants block each, and this file has to be kept in step with them by hand. The names in `${}` are the ones those blocks define (STATE_MOUNT, WORKSPACE, HOME, REPO_DIR, CLONE_DSH, CLONE_AGENTS, HARNESS_HOME, AGENTS_HOME, REPOS_DIR, WORKTREES_DIR).

backends.name: ephemeral
backends.what: The image filesystem plus container-local disk. Fast, and gone the moment the container stops.
backends.useFor: Scratch: throwaway clones, build output, temp files. Nothing here may be the only copy of anything.

backends.name: r2
backends.what: The credential-less R2 binding mount (binding STATE, bucket af-shared-tooling-dsh) at /mnt/state. It is an s3fs FUSE mount, so it is much slower than local disk.
backends.useFor: Anything that must survive a wake: installed skills, repositories, git worktrees and uncommitted work.
backends.ceiling: The SDK mounts it with stat_cache_expire=60, enable_noobj_cache and multipart_size=5, and without use_cache, so file CONTENTS are never cached locally: every read and write is a round trip to R2. Stat results are cached for 60 seconds, which is what makes a repeated `git status` cheap and a first one expensive. Adding use_cache=/tmp/... to the mount options is the identified upgrade path for git-heavy work; it is not enabled because it is unverified without a container and it trades container disk for speed. See README.md, 'What survives a wake'.

backends.name: git
backends.what: A working tree of a repository. Durable because the repository is durable, not because the container is.
backends.useFor: The harness configuration and everything the agent authors. Editable in place inside the container, reviewable and pushable back through normal git.

backends.name: volume
backends.what: DOES NOT EXIST ON THIS PLATFORM. Listed so that nobody adds it back: Cloudflare Containers provide no persistent block device, so there is no volume backend to select, and no amount of manifest editing creates one. Durability here comes from R2 and from git, and from nothing else.

paths.note: Mounted by the Worker (mountBucket) before this script runs, because a mount does not survive the container being recreated.
The clone of the tooling repository. This is the source of truth for the harness config and for the skill manifest, and it is the working tree an agent edits and commits in.

Every entry of the clone's .dsh/ is symlinked under the same name, profiles/ included. Nothing is excepted any more: the profile's node_modules is installed into the mount beside its committed manifests by `dsh-provision`, before the clone is linked, so the symlink always points at a tree that exists. A file added to the repository later arrives with no change to the script.
Supplied by the clone, not by the image. Source: .dsh/profiles in the repository, installed at run time by bin/dsh-provision.sh from the committed lockfiles.

The harness CLI, installed by `npm ci` from the committed lockfile into the mount on the FIRST run and never again. It used to be baked into the image (290 MB) and was removed: a node dependency tree is agent state, not toolchain. The marker in the mount is what makes a warm start skip the install entirely; the binary is what makes a store that lost it repair itself.

The dsh TUI and web profiles (108 MB in the image, removed for the same reason). Installed by pnpm from the frozen lockfile, ONCE. The ceiling is that these trees sit on the s3fs mount: file CONTENTS are never cached locally, so every require() is a round trip. Whether the TUI can load its bundles over s3fs is the one thing here that could not be verified without a container; if it proves too slow, the upgrade path is to copy the tree onto ephemeral disk at provision time, which is cheap because it is derived data.

A DERIVED CACHE, not a source of truth: every entry can be regenerated from the manifest with `npx skills`. It is durable because re-fetching the catalog on every wake would put a network round trip on the critical path of the operator connecting. This path is inside the clone (.agents/ maps 1:1), so an agent can also commit a skill deliberately.
Scratch. Disposable by design; never the only copy of anything.
WHERE ACTUAL WORK LIVES: clones of the repositories being worked on, with their git history, their uncommitted changes and their worktrees.

The worktree parent. GitButler is gone; `git worktree` is the isolation mechanism, so this has to be durable or worktrees are pointless. One worktree per parallel stream, named for the stream: ${WORKTREES_DIR}/<stream>.
The short, discoverable name for the same durable directory. A symlink rather than a second location: two paths to one tree is how a change gets made in the wrong one.
As above, for the worktree parent. The symlink itself is on ephemeral disk and is recreated on each cold start; the directory it points at is not.
